info.name: SalvageAlert API v1.7.0
info.description: Generated from https://salvagealert.com/api/v1/openapi.json. Set the `apiKey` collection variable to your sa_live_ key (https://salvagealert.com/app/api).

request.description: Search lots from one source. Cache hits cost 0 credits. Each source pushes down the filters its site can apply (keyword everywhere; year, damage, title and price on IAA Canada; make and year on the Copart feed; a single make on IAA US and GovDeals), and every page is then run through the same local gate the app uses, so a filter the source cannot apply still holds — the lots it removes are counted in `filtered_out`. A cache hit is never refused for balance: the pre-authorisation checks the cache first, so an account at 0 credits can still replay a cached page. A page can therefore be short or empty while `total_estimate` is large: `total_estimate` is the source's own count for the part of the request it applied, not the count after the gate. Keep paging by `page`, not by comparing lots seen to `total_estimate`.

item.name: GET /lots/{source}/{lot_key} · Fetch a single lot by stock #

request.description: Always bypasses cache so bids and sale state are live. 1 credit on a hit. On copart_us and copart_ca the source of truth is the Copart Sales Data feed we import three times a day (08:00, 14:00, 19:00 New York time), not a live page fetch, so a lot is at most a few hours old there; IAA and GovDeals lookups hit the auction live. A lot the source no longer lists — sold and removed, or withdrawn — is a 404 here even while /inventory still carries it; see `Lot.isAuctionClosed` for how to read sale status on a hit. A miss is not free: the lookup still fires a live source query, so a 404 that ran that query is charged a reduced miss fee of 1 credit. Request-shape 400s cost nothing, and so does an unsupported source, which is refused before any query runs. The exact amount is on X-Credits-Charged.

item.name: GET /lots/{source}/{lot_key}/images · List all gallery photo URLs (IAA + Copart)

request.description: Enumerate every photo the source exposes for the lot — not just the listing-page thumbnail. IAA (iaai_ca/us): enumerated from the anchor via the resizer (width/height apply); up to 50 URLs — `limit` can lower that and cannot raise it, because the enumeration walks one prefix and stops at 50. Copart (copart_ca/us/uk): full high-res set from the public gallery (fixed resolution — width/height ignored). Costs 4 credits. A miss is not free: the lookup still fires a live source query, so a 404 that ran that query is charged a reduced miss fee of 1 credit. Request-shape 400s cost nothing, and so does an unsupported source, which is refused before any query runs. The exact amount is on X-Credits-Charged.

item.name: GET /lots/{source}/{lot_key}/images.zip · Download all photos as a ZIP (IAA + Copart)

request.description: Server-built ZIP containing every photo the source exposes for the lot — IAA (iaai_ca/us, plus the exterior-360 raw frames) and Copart (copart_ca/us/uk, full high-res gallery). Up to 100 full-resolution JPEGs, fetched in parallel server-side — plus, on IAA, up to 36 exterior-360 raw frames under `360/`, so the archive can hold up to 136 entries. `X-Photos-Included` reports what actually went in. Returns application/zip with Content-Disposition attachment. Costs 8 credits. A miss is not free: the lookup still fires a live source query, so a 404 that ran that query is charged a reduced miss fee of 1 credit. Request-shape 400s cost nothing, and so does an unsupported source, which is refused before any query runs. The exact amount is on X-Credits-Charged.

Every distinct lot we have archived for a full 17-character VIN, across every source — the relisting / flip trail. Copart lots carry full, unmasked VINs across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and Germany, so cross-source matches are reliable. IAA lots carry a full VIN only where an authenticated crawl reached them. Newest first. Costs 1 credit. Returns 404 if the VIN has never been seen.

Carfax-lite title check: whether a VIN has any salvage-auction record in our IAA/Copart archive, and whether any listing carries an explicitly branded title (salvage/rebuilt/flood/junk/…). Always 200 — a missing record is a valid (clean-so-far) answer, not proof of a clean title.

1 credit when the VIN is found; a miss (`found: false`) is free, matching `/vin/{vin}/history` and `/vin/batch`.

Look up relisting history for many VINs in one call (max 50).

Charges 1 credit per VIN that RETURNED AT LEAST ONE LOT. A VIN we hold nothing for is free, exactly as /vin/{vin}/history 404s an unknown VIN at 0 credits — the same lookup costs the same through either endpoint. Malformed entries are echoed back in `invalid` and never billed.

`requested` is what you sent, `looked_up` is the valid deduped set we searched, and `billed` is the subset that had results — `billed` is what X-Credits-Charged will say. Your balance is pre-authorised for the worst case (every valid VIN a hit) before the lookups run, so a 402 means you could not have afforded the whole batch even though the real charge may be lower.

Each result mirrors the single VIN-history lot shape.

request.description:
Page through the public archived-inventory index — the same de-duplicated, continuously-crawled catalogue behind salvagealert.com/lots. Reads pre-archived stock from our index (no live source fetch). Costs 1 credit per call.

**Two pagination modes. Only one of them is safe for bulk.**

`page` is an OFFSET into a table the poller and three crawlers write to continuously. It is correct for jumping to a page a person will read, and wrong for mirroring: at page_size=100 a full walk of the catalogue is thousands of requests, rows shift underneath it throughout, and the walk silently skips and duplicates lots. It is capped at page 500.

`cursor` is the keyset mode and is what you want for a mirror. Results are ordered by (archived_at, source, lot_key) ascending; pass the `next_cursor` from the previous response to resume, and stop when it comes back null. A lot the crawler re-touches mid-walk moves to the END of that ordering — which the walk has not reached — so it is re-emitted rather than skipped. Send `cursor` or `updated_since` (or both) to select this mode; `page` and `sort` are then ignored, because the ordering IS the cursor.

`updated_since` (unix SECONDS, compared against `archived_at`) is the incremental half: having mirrored once, ask only for what has changed rather than re-walking the whole catalogue at a credit a page. Combine it with `cursor` to page through a large delta. `archived_at` moves whenever a lot CHANGES — bid, sale date, photo, identity, a sale — and not on a re-crawl that found it unchanged, so a delta is exactly the lots whose details changed plus those new to you; upsert on (source, lot_key). With `include_sold=true` the delta also carries the lots that sold since, each with its `sold_at`.

Lots deleted from our catalogue are NOT reported by this endpoint — a mirror should treat a lot it has not seen for a while as stale rather than expecting a tombstone.

**Ended lots are opt-in.** By default the endpoint returns live stock only, so every row has `sold_at` null. Send `include_sold=true` to receive the ended archive too: lots that sold, and lots the source stopped listing without a sale we could record. The second kind can carry a null `sold_at`, so treat a `sale_date_utc` in the past as ended rather than reading `sold_at` alone. It works in both pagination modes and combines with `updated_since`, since a sale moves `archived_at`. What it never returns is a lot a SalvageAlert account holder hid from their own view — a lot OUR crawler simply stopped seeing is catalogue history, and is returned.

As of 2026-09-02 each lot also carries acv, title_state, origin_country, sale_event_status, sale_light, autograde, make_offer, wholesale_only, former_rental, offsite/offsite_location, lane, run_number, airbags_status, loss_type, has_keys, drives, starts and trim — additive, so existing integrations are unaffected. As of 2026-09-04 it also carries high_prebid_value, buy_now_value and sold_at, so prices can be sorted and charted without parsing the formatted current_bid/buy_now strings, and an ended lot can be told from a live one.

item.name: GET /inventory/{source}/{lot_key} · One archived lot by identity

request.description: A single lot from the catalogue, off the index — the same InventoryLot shape `/inventory` pages through, for every one of the eight sources. No live source fetch: this is the read for a mirror re-checking a lot it already holds, or for resolving a `(source, lot_key)` a webhook delivered. 1 credit on a hit, nothing on a miss; an index lookup is not a scrape, so a 404 is not a fee. For the freshest bid straight from the auction house, `/lots/{source}/{lot_key}` still asks live.
Live active-lot counts per source in the archived-inventory index. Use it to discover how much stock each source has available before paging /inventory. 0 credits.

Every upcoming IAA USA, IAA Canada and Copart sale the worker has read, one chronological list sorted by start. A Copart sale carries its `yard` in the spelling /inventory?yard= takes and `catalog_lots`, how many lots we hold there with a sale in the next eight days. `copart_stale` says the Copart list is older than we trust; check Copart's own calendar before planning around it. `iaai_us_upcoming_days` lists days IAA USA advertises without their lots. Stored rows, refreshed by the worker; nothing is scraped on your call. 0 credits.
Your account, live credit balance and current per-minute rate limit. 0 credits.
Per-day and per-endpoint counts for the last N days (max 90).
Every key on the account, live and revoked, masked to its display prefix. `current` marks the key this call was made with. Free.

item.name: POST /api-keys · Mint a new API key

request.description: Issues one more key without touching the others — a second service, a staging box, a key per customer. The raw secret is returned ONCE. `project_url` is where the key is called from and is required unless a live key on the account already names one, in which case it is carried over. An account may hold 20 active keys. Free. To replace every key at once, see /api-keys/rotate.
Revokes a single key. The calling key may revoke itself — the response lands and the next call with it is a 401. Free.

**Privileged and irreversible.** Revokes EVERY active key on the account — not just the one that made this call — and mints a single fresh key. The raw secret is returned ONCE and cannot be retrieved again; only its hash and display prefix are stored.

Any other integration still holding an older key starts receiving 401 `invalid_credentials` immediately, so on a multi-key account this is a deploy, not a maintenance task.

It costs 0 credits and requires no re-authentication beyond the bearer key itself, which means a leaked key can rotate the account and lock out its legitimate owner. The account owner is emailed on every rotation — if you receive that mail and did not rotate, rotate again to cut the holder off and check your API usage log.

item.name: PATCH /matches/{id} · Favorite, dismiss, annotate or price a match

request.description:
Writes your decisions on a matched lot: favorite or un-favorite it, dismiss or restore it, set or clear the ceiling (`max_bid_value`) that the max-bid alert and `max_bid_crossed` webhook fire on, the Buy Now target (`price_alert_value`) behind `price_drop`, a private note, and the won and resale prices the won ledger and margin read. Free.

Send only the fields you want changed — an omitted field is left alone; `null` clears a price or the note. Sending nothing is a 400. The ceiling and the target are favorites features, so set `favorited: true` in the same body if the lot is not one yet; `resale_price` needs a won lot. Returns the full updated Match.

request.description:
Streams your saved-search match history as a CSV download, drawn only from your own searches. Free — the data was paid for at poll time; reading it back is a download, not a scrape. Up to 50,000 rows per call, newest first.

**Timestamps in the file are ISO-8601 UTC strings** (`2026-01-15T09:00:00.000Z`) — every one of them, including `sale_date_utc`, which is an epoch integer everywhere else on this API. That is the only representation a spreadsheet opens as a date, and this endpoint exists to be opened in one. The `since` and `until` QUERY parameters are still epoch seconds, because they are API inputs rather than file contents. See `x-conventions`.

item.name: GET /models · Model list for a make

request.description:
The shape of `yards` depends on the source, so switch on `source` before reading it.

- `copart_ca`, `copart_us` — physical yards: `{ code, name, region }`, where region is the province or state, uppercase.
- `iaai_ca` — the .NET provincial branch catalogue: `{ id, name, province }`. Note `id` is a NUMBER and there is no `code`; a client written against the Copart shape reads undefined here.
- `iaai_uk`, `iaai_us`, `copart_uk`, `copart_de`, `govdeals_us` — `yards` is an empty array and a `note` explains what to pass to /lots/search instead. This is the documented answer for those sources, not a failure or an empty catalogue.

0 credits.

The HMAC `secret` is returned exactly once on creation and cannot be retrieved afterwards.

The URL must be absolute https — plain http is refused with `non_https`. It is validated on creation AND re-validated at every delivery, so a host that later resolves into a private range stops being delivered to: private / RFC1918 / loopback / cloud-metadata addresses are refused (`private_address`), as are unresolvable hosts (`dns_unresolvable`), URLs carrying `user:pass@` (`credentials_in_url`) and anything unparseable (`invalid_url`). A URL that starts failing this check counts toward the 20-failure auto-disable like any other failure.

`format` defaults to whatever your URL looks like — see the Webhook schema, and note that a Discord or Slack URL disables HMAC signing.

Partial update. Sending `{"active": true}` is how you bring back a subscription that was auto-disabled after 20 consecutive failures — fix the receiver first, because the counter is not reset until a delivery actually succeeds. Changing `url` re-runs the same SSRF validation as creation. The `secret` is never re-issued here; rotate the webhook by deleting and recreating it if you need a new one.

Synchronous one-shot delivery for testing your receiver. Not persisted to the deliveries log; not retried on failure. It is shaped like a real delivery: event `webhook.test`, `data.kind` = `test`, the same 15 s timeout, and an `X-Salvagealert-Delivery-Id` header carrying the `delivery_id` returned here.

Rate-limited to 6 per minute PER WEBHOOK, on top of the account allowance: this is the one endpoint that makes an outbound request on your word, and it holds the connection open for up to 15 seconds.

Recent deliveries for a webhook, newest first. Use it to self-debug a failing receiver without contacting support — and to see how close a subscription is to the 20-failure auto-disable. Statuses: `pending` (queued or awaiting its next backoff attempt), `delivered` (a 2xx), `failed` (permanently refused — a non-retryable 4xx, or a URL that failed re-validation), `dead` (all 7 attempts exhausted, or dropped because the subscription was disabled). 0 credits.

Queue a failed, dead or delivered delivery again: same payload, a fresh attempt count, sent on the worker's next drain (within a minute). A `pending` delivery is refused with 409 — it is already on its way. Rate-limited to 20 per minute per account, since it makes an outbound request to a URL you control. 0 credits.
Every VIN watch on the account, each with the lots it has found and its event trail (listed, sold, listed again). 0 credits.

Watch one vehicle. Passively, every lot ingested on any source is checked against the VIN and a hit sends a `lot.matched` delivery of kind `vin_watch_match`; with a `region` and `sources` the watch also runs the VIN as a keyword search on those sources every 48 h (or on demand with /run). The watch survives relistings — it keys on the VIN, not the lot number — and after a hit it reports the sale and any return in `events`. The VIN is fixed at creation. One watch per VIN per account (409 `duplicate`); at most 200 watches (429 `too_many_watches`); a plan without VIN watches is refused with 403 `plan_gate`. 0 credits.

item.name: PATCH /vin-watches/{id} · Pause, resume or edit a VIN watch

request.description: Send only the fields you want changed: `active`, `label`, `region`, `sources`. Omitted fields are left alone; an empty body is a 400. The VIN cannot be changed. Returns the full updated watch. 0 credits.

item.name: POST /vin-watches/{id}/run · Run a VIN watch now

request.description: Run the watch's keyword sweep inline on the sources it names and return what it found. Needs a region and sources. Once per 24 h per watch (429 `cooldown` with `retry_after_s`), since a sweep is a live source query. 0 API credits.

Saved filter set that triggers `lot.matched` events (kind `watch_match`). filters JSON is capped at 4 KB — over it, 400 `watch_filters_too_large`.

To pause a watch, PATCH it with `{"active": false}` and PATCH it back when you want it firing again — the id survives, so anything you correlate on it keeps working. `active` is YOURS ALONE: nothing on the server ever clears it. A `vin_watch_match` delivery comes from the per-VIN watches, a different feature that stands itself down once it finds its vehicle; those live under /vin-watches.

`source` and `filters` are fixed at creation. They define what the watch IS, so changing them would repoint an id you are already correlating on — POST a new watch instead.

WHAT A WATCH SEES: lots as they are INGESTED BY A SAVED SEARCH — this account's or any other's. It is not the whole catalogue. The bulk imports that also fill it (the daily Copart sales feed, the archive crawl, the Buy Now crawl) do not fan out to watches, so a lot that only ever arrives that way appears in `/v1/inventory` without ever having triggered a watch. Poll `/v1/inventory` with `updated_since` when you need every lot; use a watch when you want to be told about the ones people are actively tracking.

item.name: PATCH /watches/{id} · Pause, resume or relabel a watch

request.description:
Updates `active` and/or `label` in place. Free.

Send only the fields you want changed — an omitted field is left alone, so `{"active": false}` will not blank the label. Sending neither is a 400 rather than a silent no-op. Returns the full updated Watch.

`source` and `filters` cannot be patched; see POST /watches.

Decode a 17-character VIN into a structured vehicle spec: year, make, model, trim, body class, engine, drivetrain, transmission, plant and more. Pass ?year= to disambiguate pre-2010 VINs. Costs 0.2 credits.

Open recall campaigns plus crash-test safety ratings for a year/make/model. Costs 0.2 credits.

**`recalls.count: 0` means no OPEN recalls, and only for a model NHTSA recognises.** A model name it does not list — a typo, or a market-specific name — answers 404 `no_match` rather than zero recalls, which would read as a clean bill of health for a car that does not exist. `model_recognized` reports which of the two you have: `true` confirmed, `null` when NHTSA's own model catalogue could not be read (the recall and rating figures still stand).

**Ratings are per variant.** NCAP rates each body/drivetrain variant separately ("2018 HONDA ACCORD 4 DR FWD"), and `ratings` describes the FIRST one NHTSA lists, named in `ratings.variant`. `rated_variants` carries every variant it rates for that year/make/model, so a caller looking at a specific trim can see whether the stars belong to it.

query.description: Pick one of the trims in `trims` (case-insensitive, exact match first, then substring). Omit to use the first the EPA lists. An unmatched trim is 404 `no_match`, never a silent fall back to another trim.

request.description:
EPA MPG, fuel type, CO2 and estimated annual fuel cost for a year/make/model. Costs 0.2 credits.

**The EPA rates trims, not models.** A 2020 Camry is 39 MPG combined as a 4-cylinder and 26 as a V6, and they are separate records. Pass `trim` to pick one (matched case-insensitively, exact first then as a substring); without it the FIRST record the EPA lists is used, which is menu order and not "the usual one". `trims` returns every trim available for that year/make/model so the choice can be made explicitly, and `trim` names the one the figures describe.

**Zero is a value.** `co2_g_per_mile: 0` on a battery-electric car is its tailpipe emission, not a missing reading; unknown figures are `null`.

query.description: Comma-separated target currency codes.

request.description: Daily reference exchange rates for converting auction prices across the currencies SalvageAlert lots trade in. Defaults to USD base against USD, EUR, CAD and GBP. Costs 0.2 credits.

query.description: Optional model filter.

request.description:
Aggregate price snapshot for a make (and optional model) across the whole archive. Costs 1 credit.

**What the price actually is.** Each distinct lot — one row per (source, lot number) — contributes its Buy Now price if it has one, otherwise its highest pre-bid, converted to USD at the current reference rate. That is the best price we hold for the lot, NOT a confirmed sale price: most salvage lots sell on approval and the hammer price is never published, so nothing here is a "winning bid". Treat it as the asking/bidding level, not the settlement.

**Which lots each number counts.** `lot_count` is every distinct lot matching the make/model, priced or not. `avg_bid`, `median_bid`, `min_bid` and `max_bid` are computed over the SUBSET that carries a price above zero, which is smaller and is not currently returned — so `avg_bid × lot_count` is not a market total. `avg_retail_value` is likewise averaged only over lots carrying a pre-loss retail estimate. `median_bid` is the lower of the two middle values on an even count. No outlier trimming is applied: a mistyped 9,999,999 bid in a feed moves `max_bid` and `avg_bid` and leaves `median_bid` alone, which is why the median is the number to build on.

query.description: Canadian province (QC, ON, AB, BC, MB, SK, NB, NS, NL or PE) for iaai_ca / copart_ca, or a US state (FL, TX, … incl. DC) for iaai_us / copart_us / govdeals_us. Validated against the source's country: a region the market cannot charge is refused with `invalid_tax_region` rather than applied by name.
Set 0 to omit PST/GST.

Accepted and currently IGNORED. No schedule we hold splits its buyer fee by payment method — the Copart Canada tables that once did were unsourced and removed — so the estimate is identical either way. It stays in the contract because clients send it; it will start moving the number only if a market

How the lot is acquired. `preBid` and `liveBid` select the house's internet bid fee column. `buyNow` is a purchase at the listed price, which is not an awarded bid, so no internet or proxy bid fee line is charged at all — send it when you are pricing a Buy Now lot, or the estimate overstates the cos
A motorcycle, ATV, snowmobile, jet ski, boat or RV. In Quebec the auction then charges QST on the sale price as well as the fees; a road vehicle's QST on its price is paid at registration instead.

request.description: All-in buyer-fee breakdown for a hammer price on any marketplace we cover (IAA CA/US/UK, Copart CA/US/UK/DE). Pure calculation — no scrape. Returns the itemized fee lines plus optional PST/GST. Costs 0.2 credits.
